FIRST LIGHT FROM THE EAST: pale rose and gold seeping over the horizon, long lavender shadows stretching westward across the dock planks, edges touched with soft apricot warmth
DAWN GLOW FROM THE SOUTHEAST: thin golden light raking low across the waterside path, shadows long and cool lilac, every timber grain illuminated in warm blush amber
EARLY DAWN FROM THE EAST: a gentle wash of peach and pale yellow spreads from the right, shadows trail long and mauve toward the left, horizon rimmed in coral
FIRST LIGHT OVERHEAD: soft diffuse rose light descending from a brightening sky, shadows short and tender pink, the whole scene bathed in a quiet warm haze of dawn
DAWN EDGE FROM THE NORTHEAST: pale lemony gold arrives at a low angle, casting long diagonal lavender shadows across the planks, warm amber light defining every raised surface edge
GOLDEN EVENING FROM THE WEST: low warm sun from the left, long amber shadows across the planks, every edge rimmed in gold and the path glowing deep honey
LATE GOLDEN HOUR FROM THE SOUTHWEST: rich amber light floods in at a low left angle, shadows rake long and burnt sienna to the right, surfaces lit in molten copper
EVENING SUN FROM THE WEST: deep golden orange light from the far left, long warm shadows streaking rightward across dock boards, every upward face blazing in tangerine and gold
GOLDEN DUSK FROM THE WEST: the sun sits just above the horizon to the left, flooding the path in rich caramel light, shadows long and deep umber trailing eastward
LATE AFTERNOON FROM THE NORTHWEST: slanted amber light enters from the upper left, warm honey tones across horizontal surfaces, long cool ochre shadows angling toward the lower right
BLUE HOUR AT DUSK: the sun just gone, cool indigo light from the whole sky, one last warm band along the western edge, shadows soft and blue pooling in every hollow
DEEP DUSK FROM THE WEST: residual warm violet on the western horizon, the rest of the scene bathed in cool blue-grey, shadows nearly indistinguishable, soft purple tones across all flat surfaces
BLUE HOUR OVERHEAD: even cool sapphire light descending from the zenith, shadows faint and blue-grey, a fading amber glow persisting low on the western side, surfaces rendered in cool teal silver
EARLY DUSK FROM THE WEST: a thin band of warm peach low on the left horizon, the main light shifting to cool periwinkle from above, shadows gentle and deep violet
TWILIGHT BLUE FROM THE SKY: full blue hour, even cool indigo descending from above, the western edge still holding a pale gold ribbon, shadows soft lavender merging gently into the ground
FULL MOON FROM ABOVE: cold white-silver light pouring straight down, hard crisp shadows of deep blue-black beneath every post and plank edge, surfaces gleaming in pale icy luminescence
MOONLIGHT FROM THE EAST: silver light enters low from the right, long cool grey-blue shadows stretching leftward, every upward surface traced in cold platinum and the path shimmering faintly

HIGH MOONLIGHT FROM THE SOUTH: bright cool white moon overhead and slightly south, short blue-grey shadows falling northward, timber surfaces glowing silver and pale steel, scene rendered in monochrome serenity
MOONLIGHT FROM THE WEST: cold silver illumination coming from the left at a low angle, long stark shadows of cobalt blue trailing rightward, every edge sharp and bright as polished tin
SOFT OVERCAST SILVER FROM ABOVE: even diffuse grey-white light from the whole sky, shadows nearly absent, a gentle silver sheen across all horizontal surfaces, tones cool and uniformly pale
SILVER OVERCAST MIDDAY: flat cool silver light descending evenly, minimal shadow depth, surfaces rendered in muted grey and soft white, the entire path feeling calm and tonally unified
OVERCAST SILVER MORNING: pale cool white light from an even sky above, shadows faint and barely visible, surfaces touched in cool grey-lavender, the scene quiet and gently luminous

CLEAR MIDDAY FROM ABOVE: strong white sunlight straight down from the zenith, short hard shadows directly beneath every post and rail, surfaces bleached bright and edges sharply defined in stark contrast

HIGH NOON FULL SUN: intense clear yellow-white light from directly overhead, minimal shadow footprint tight beneath each object, all upward surfaces blazing in bright warm white, colours fully saturated
MIDDAY SUN FROM THE SOUTH: bright clear sunlight from slightly south of overhead, short crisp shadows angling just northward, all surfaces lit in clean warm white with strong sharp contrast
